readings.subsection: The Covenant of Daviḏ and Yehonathan
readings.title: Daviḏ Flees to Yehonathan
readings.subtitle: The Plan to Test Sha’ul's Intentions
readings.text:
[1 Samuel 20:1] And Daviḏ fled from Navith in Ramah, and went and said to Yehonathan, “What have I done? What is my crookedness, and what is my sin before your father, that he seeks <dn>את</dn> my life?”
[2] And Yehonathan said to him, “Far be it! You are not going to die! See, my father does no big matter nor small matter without disclosing it to me. And why should my father hide <dn>את</dn> this matter from me? It is not so!”
[3] But Daviḏ swore again, and said, “Your father knows well that I have found favour in your eyes, and he says, ‘Do not let Yehonathan know this, lest he be grieved.’ But truly, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives and as your being lives, there is but a step between me and death.”
[4] And Yehonathan said to Daviḏ, “Whatever your desire is, I do it for you.”
[5] And Daviḏ said to Yehonathan, “See, tomorrow is the new moon, and I ought to sit with the sovereign to eat. But let me go, and I shall hide in the field until the third day at evening.
[6] “If your father misses me at all, then you shall say, ‘Daviḏ earnestly asked my permission to run over to Běyth Leḥem, his city, for a yearly slaughtering is made there for all the clan.’
[7] “If he says thus, ‘It is well,’ your servant is safe. But if he is very displeased, then know that he has resolved to do evil.
[8] “And you shall show loving-commitment to your servant, for you have brought <dn>את</dn> your servant into a covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> with you. And if there is crookedness in me, put me to death yourself, for why should you bring me to your father?”
[9] And Yehonathan said, “Far be it from you! For if I knew with certainty that my father has resolved that evil is to come upon you, then would I not make it known to you?”
[10] And Daviḏ said to Yehonathan, “Who would make it known to me, or what if your father answers you sharply?”
[11] And Yehonathan said to Daviḏ, “Come, and let us go out into the field.” And they both went out into the field.
[12] And Yehonathan said to Daviḏ, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl be witness! When I search out <dn>את</dn> my father sometime tomorrow, or the third day, and see if there is good toward Daviḏ, and I do not send to you or disclose it to you,
[13] so let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> do so and much more to Yehonathan. And if it pleases my father to do you evil, then I shall disclose it to you and send you away, and you shall go in peace. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> be with you as <dn>He</dn> has been with my father.
[14] “But show me the loving-commitment of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, not only while I still live, so that I do not die,
[15] and do not cut off <dn>את</dn> your loving-commitment from my house forever, no, not when <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has cut off <dn>את</dn> every one of the enemies of Daviḏ from the face of the earth.”
[16] And Yehonathan made a covenant with the house of Daviḏ, saying, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall require it at the hand of the enemies of Daviḏ.”
[17] And Yehonathan again made <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ swear, because he loved him, for he loved him as he loved his own being.
[18] So Yehonathan said to him, “Tomorrow is the new moon, and you shall be missed, because your seat shall be empty.
[19] “And on the third day, go down quickly and you shall come to the place where you hid on the day of the deed, and shall remain by the stone Ětsel.
[20] “And let me shoot three arrows to the side of it as though shooting at a target,
[21] and see, I shall send <dn>את</dn> the youth, saying, ‘Go, find <dn>את</dn> the arrows.’ If I expressly say to the youth, ‘Look, the arrows are on this side of you, get them and come,’ then, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives, there is safety for you and no concern.
[22] “But if I say thus to the youth, ‘Look, the arrows are beyond you,’ go your way, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has sent you away.
[23] “And as for the word which you and I have spoken of, see, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is between you and me forever.”
[24] And Daviḏ hid in the field. And when the new moon came, the sovereign sat down by the food to eat.
[25] And the sovereign sat on his seat, as at other times, on a seat by the wall, with Yehonathan standing, and Aḇněr sitting by Sha’ul’s side, but the place of Daviḏ was empty.
[26] But Sha’ul spoke not a word that day, for he thought, “It is an accident; he is not clean, for he has not been cleansed.”
[27] And it came to be the next day, the second day of the new moon, that Daviḏ’s place was empty. And Sha’ul said to Yehonathan his son, “Why has the son of Yishai not come to eat, either yesterday or today?”
[28] And Yehonathan answered <dn>את</dn> Sha’ul, “Daviḏ earnestly asked my permission to go to Běyth Leḥem.
[29] “And he said, ‘Please let me go, for our clan has a slaughtering in the city, and my brother has commanded me to be there. And now, if I have found favour in your eyes, please let me get away and see <dn>את</dn> my brothers.’ That is why he has not come to the sovereign’s table.”
[30] Then the displeasure of Sha’ul burned against Yehonathan, and he said to him, “You son of a perverse, rebellious woman! Do I not know that you have chosen the son of Yishai to your own shame and to the shame of your mother’s nakedness?
[31] “For as long as the son of Yishai lives on the earth, you shall not be established, you and your reign. And now, send and bring <dn>את</dn> him to me, for he is a son of death.”
[32] And Yehonathan answered <dn>את</dn> Sha’ul his father, and said to him, “Why should he be put to death? What has he done?”
[33] At that, Sha’ul hurled <dn>את</dn> a spear at him to smite him. Then Yehonathan knew that his father had resolved to put <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ to death.
[34] And Yehonathan rose up from the table in the heat of displeasure, and ate no food the second day of the new moon, for he was grieved for Daviḏ, because his father put him to shame.
[35] And it came to be, in the morning, that Yehonathan went out into the field at the time appointed with Daviḏ, and a small youth was with him.
[36] And he said to the youth, “Now run, find <dn>את</dn> the arrows which I shoot.” As the youth ran, he shot an arrow beyond him.
[37] And when the youth came to the place where the arrow was which Yehonathan had shot, Yehonathan called out after the youth and said, “Is not the arrow beyond you?”
[38] And Yehonathan shouted after the youth, “Make haste, hurry, do not stand still!” And Yehonathan’s youth picked up <dn>את</dn> the arrows and came to his master.
[39] But the youth knew not a speck. Only Yehonathan and Daviḏ knew <dn>את</dn> of the matter.
[40] Then Yehonathan gave <dn>את</dn> his weapons to the youth and said to him, “Go, take them to the city.”
[41] And as soon as the youth had gone, Daviḏ rose up from the south side, and fell on his face to the ground, and bowed down three times. And they kissed <dn>את</dn> one another. And they wept together, but Daviḏ more so.
[42] And Yehonathan said to Daviḏ, “Go in peace, since we have both sworn in the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, ‘<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is between you and me, and between your seed and my seed, forever.’ ” Then he arose and left, and Yehonathan went into the city.

readings.title: Daviḏ Flees to Noḇ
readings.subtitle: The Set-Apart Bread
readings.text:
[1 Samuel 21:1] And Daviḏ came to Noḇ, to Aḥimeleḵ the priest. And Aḥimeleḵ trembled when he met Daviḏ, and asked him, “Why are you alone, and no one is with you?”
[2] And Daviḏ said to Aḥimeleḵ the priest, “The sovereign has commanded me a word, and said to me, ‘Let no one know whatever of the word about which I send you, and which I have commanded you.’ And I have directed <dn>את</dn> my young men to such and such a place.
[3] “And now, what do you have on hand? Give five loaves into my hand, or whatever is found.”
[4] And the priest answered <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ and said, “There is no ordinary bread on hand, but there is set-apart bread – provided the young men have kept themselves from women.”
[5] And Daviḏ answered <dn>את</dn> the priest, and said to him, “Truly, women have been kept from us about three days since I came out. And the vessels of the young men are set-apart, and it is an ordinary mission, and also, it was set-apart in the vessel today.”
[6] Then the priest gave him set-apart bread, for there was no bread there except the showbread which had been taken from before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, in order to put hot bread in on the day it is taken away.
[7] Now one of the servants of Sha’ul was there that day, detained before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And his name was Do’ěḡ, an Eḏomite, the chief of the herdsmen who belonged to Sha’ul.
[8] And Daviḏ said to Aḥimeleḵ, “Is there not here on hand a spear or a sword? For I have brought neither my sword nor <dn>את</dn> my weapons with me, because the matter of the sovereign was urgent.”
[9] And the priest said, “The sword of Golyath the Philistine, whom you struck in the Valley of Ělah. See, it is wrapped in a garment behind the shoulder garment. If you would take it, take it. For there is none other except this one here.” And Daviḏ said, “There is none like it, give it to me.”

readings.title: Daviḏ Flees to Gath
readings.subtitle: Feigning Madness Before Aḵish
readings.text:
[10] And Daviḏ rose and fled that day from before Sha’ul, and went to Aḵish the sovereign of Gath.
[11] But the servants of Aḵish said to him, “Is this not Daviḏ the sovereign of the land? Did they not sing of him to each other in dances, saying, ‘Sha’ul struck his thousands, and Daviḏ his ten thousands’?”
[12] And Daviḏ took <dn>את</dn> these words to heart, and was very much afraid of Aḵish the sovereign of Gath,
[13] and changed <dn>את</dn> his behaviour before them, and feigned madness in their hands, and scratched on the doors of the gate, and let his saliva run down on his beard.
[14] Then Aḵish said to his servants, “Look, you see the man is acting like a madman. Why do you bring <dn>את</dn> him to me?
[15] “Am I short of madmen, that you have brought <dn>את</dn> this one to act as a madman near me? Should this one come into my house?”

readings.title: A Psalm of Praise for Deliverance
readings.subtitle: When Daviḏ Feigned Madness Before Aḇimeleḵ
readings.text:
[Psalm 34:1] Aleph I bless <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> at all times; <dn>His</dn> praise is continually in my mouth.
[2] Bět My being makes its boast in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>; Let the humble hear and be glad.
[3] Gimel Oh, make <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> great with me, And let us exalt <dn>His</dn> Name together.
[4] Dalet I sought <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>He</dn> answered me, And delivered me from all my fears.
[5] Hě They looked to <dn>Him</dn> and were lightened, Waw And their faces were not ashamed.
[6] Zayin This poor one cried out and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> heard him, And saved him out of all his distresses.
[7] Ḥet The messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> encamps all around those who fear <dn>Him</dn>, And rescues them.
[8] Tet Oh, taste and see that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is good; Blessed is the man that takes refuge in <dn>Him</dn>!
[9] Yod Fear <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, you <dn>His</dn> set-apart ones, For there is no lack to them who fear <dn>Him</dn>!
[10] Kaph Young lions have lacked and been hungry; But those who seek <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lack not any good matter.
[11] Lamed Come, you children, listen to me; Let me teach you the fear of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[12] Mem Who is the man who desires life, Who loves many days, in order to see good?
[13] Nun Keep your tongue from evil, And your lips from speaking deceit.
[14] Sameḵ Turn away from evil and do good; Seek peace, and pursue it.
[15] Ayin The eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> are on the righteous, And <dn>His</dn> ears unto their cry.
[16] Pě The face of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is against evil-doers, To cut off their remembrance from the earth.
[17] Tsadi The righteous cried out, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> heard, And delivered them out of all their distresses.
[18] Qoph <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is near to the broken-hearted, And saves those whose spirit is crushed.
[19] Rěsh Many are the evils of the righteous, But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> delivers him out of them all.
[20] Shin <dn>He</dn> is guarding all his bones; Not one of them is broken.
[21] Tav Evil does slay the wrong, And those who hate the righteous are guilty.
[22] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> redeems the lives of <dn>His</dn> servants, And none of those taking refuge in <dn>Him</dn> are guilty.
